claim: Birth parent 6-week (42-day) convalescent period is counted inside the 84 days of parental leave

claim: Convalescent leave is no longer a fixed 42 days and is separate from parental leave (MARADMIN 129/23)
quote: It is separate and distinct from parental leave.

claim: The 84-day secondary caregiver entitlement reflects the interim increase issued under PAA 01-22

claim: Summary frames the entitlement as for primary or secondary caregivers

claim: A new qualifying event inside the window triggers a new 84-day entitlement and forfeits the unused portion of the prior event

claim: MARADMIN 051/23 and 129/23 are the cited authority for Active Component MPLP, now consolidated into MCO 1050.3J per MARADMIN 191/26

claim: Pregnancy notification is required of the birth parent and MARADMIN 111/23 is now incorporated into MCO 1050.3J
quote: is encouraged to notify appropriate command authorities ... no later than 20 weeks gestation

claim: Parental leave is granted during PCS and members must not exceed available entitlement or excess delay en route comes from annual leave

claim: Documentation of the qualifying event is required per MARADMIN 111/23
quote: UPDATE TO PREGNANCY NOTIFICATION

quote: The processes and procedures defined herein supersede the processes and procedures defined in reference (c).

claim: MARADMIN 545/26 reopened SLA under three categories
quote: eligibility for SLA in FY26 is authorized under the following categories

quote: leave accumulated in excess of 60 days shall be lost at the end of the fiscal year

claim: Day of departure after half a duty day is not chargeable, day of return is chargeable unless before normal work hours or 0800 on weekend or holiday
quote: when such departure is prior to half a duty day, then the day of departure is chargeable as leave

claim: Leave program includes at least one period of about 14 consecutive days each year
quote: at least one leave period each year of approximately 14-consecutive days in length

quote: will only be charged leave for those days that are duty days.

claim: No more than 60 days annual leave per FY and no continuous period over 60 days without CMC approval

quote: becomes excess leave and is subject to checkage of pay and allowances

claim: Recalled Marine is reimbursed non-refundable leave expenses per the JTR
quote: the period of absence shall not be charged to the leave account ... is 3-days or less

claim: Absence over leave is unauthorized absence
quote: Absence over authorized leave, if determined to be unavoidable, shall be charged to the Marine’s leave account

claim: Advance leave has no stated cap: chain of command sets it, and over 30 days needs higher approval by local policy
quote: advance leave shall be limited to the lesser of: (1) 45 days or (2) The amount of leave that shall be earned
fix: State the limit. MCO 1050.3J caps advance leave at the lesser of 45 days or leave earnable in the remaining enlistment. DoDI 1327.06 CH 1 para 3.11.b normally sets 30 days and sends anything over 30 days to the Secretary of the Military Department. Reconcile with the 30-day DoDI figure.

claim: Advance leave over 30 days needs higher chain of command approval based on local policy
quote: Advance leave exceeding 30 days will be authorized by the Secretary of the Military Department concerned
fix: Approval above 30 days is a Department of the Navy decision, not a unit policy matter.

claim: Excess leave is without pay and allowances
quote: No pay and allowance entitlements are authorized while in an excess leave status.

claim: Excess leave does not count toward retirement, BAH stops and TRICARE continuation is affected
quote: Leave accrual stops on the first day of excess leave.
fix: No source in the cluster addresses retirement credit, BAH or TRICARE during excess leave, and 10 USC 701 is the leave accrual statute. Remove or source from the FMR and Title 10 service-credit rules. State what the order says: pay, allowances and leave accrual stop.

claim: Excess leave applies when the Marine has no accrued balance and is not earning fast enough, with no mention of the 60-day aggregate limit
quote: Excess leave may be granted in emergencies provided the aggregate of all leave granted (accrued, advance, and excess) does not exceed 60 days.
fix: Add the 60-day aggregate limit and the rule requiring advance leave before excess leave. Excess leave is leave beyond what is earnable before the expiration of current contract.

claim: Unearned advance leave at separation is recouped as daily basic pay rate times days
quote: collection, if applicable, of daily value of pay and allowances paid to a Service member for each day of excess leave
fix: Collection is the daily value of pay and allowances, not basic pay alone.

claim: Recoupment exemptions per Vol 7A Chapter 2 Table 2-1 (death, combat disability, hardship discharge)
fix: DoD 7000.14-R Vol 7A Ch 2 is not in the cluster archive. Verify against the FMR.

claim: Advance leave is paid leave and pay and allowances continue

claim: Initial convalescent leave is typically 30 days and extensions are decided by the medical authority
quote: Convalescent leave in excess of 30 days shall be coordinated with the CMC (MMEA/MMOA, or RA, as applicable).

claim: Only the medical authority can authorize or extend convalescent leave and the command cannot

claim: Active Component birth parents receive a 6-week convalescent period counted within the 84-day MPLP entitlement
quote: The 12 weeks of ADPL is in addition to any period of convalescent leave for the recovery of a Service member from giving birth.

claim: Standard emergency leave authority is up to 30 days and extensions need chain of command approval
quote: leave granting authorities may authorize emergency leave for a period greater than 60 days without approval of the CMC (MMEA/MMOA).

claim: American Red Cross verification is required for OCONUS Marines requesting funded leave travel

claim: Marines do not have a separate bereavement leave entitlement

claim: The S-1 officer signs by direction on emergency leave per MCO 1050.3J
quote: the commander or designated official (Leave Manager) is authorized to sign the Leave Authorization (NAVMC 3).
fix: The order allows the commander or a designated Leave Manager to sign. It does not mention by direction signature. Reword to designated official.

claim: SLA review for leave lost at fiscal year end follows MARADMIN 545/26
quote: will review all pending and previously held or returned SLA packages against the designated units list posted on the MPO website.

claim: Approved SLA restores lost days and every held package is reviewed
quote: On 30 October 2026, the Marine’s SLA was adjusted to reflect the restored days

claim: Use PDMRA before annual leave to avoid credit loss
quote: PDMRA is a use or lose entitlement. It shall be used prior to a Marine’s EAS or deactivation
fix: PDMRA is use or lose before EAS, component change, retirement or the next PCS. The order sets no rule to use it ahead of annual leave. Reword to the actual deadline.

claim: PDMRA transactions are non-chargeable absence yet outputs include a chargeable status entry
quote: PDMRA is authorized to Marines who are deployed/mobilized at less than the deployment-dwell ratio, 1:2 for the active component
fix: PDMRA is administrative absence and is non-chargeable. Remove the chargeable status entry output.

claim: Eligibility and creditable time follow Chapter 6 paragraphs 2 and 3
quote: The minimum duration of initial deployment to the area of responsibility (AOR) is four consecutive months (120-consecutive days) to be eligible for PDMRA.

claim: Unused PDMRA credit is lost at expiration and the S-1 chief tracks it
quote: Failure to use PDMRA days within the designated time frame will result in loss of the benefit

claim: Special R&R (paragraph 14) applies additional rules per qualifying operation and the deployed commander selects R&R or Special R&R
quote: may elect to receive either a monthly extension bonus for the period of the extension or 30 days special leave
fix: SR&R is the overseas tour extension incentive. It is not tied to an operation and the Marine elects it. MARADMIN 450/26 now sets 30 days, or 15 days (20 for extensions of 13 months or more) with round-trip transportation. Rewrite and cite 450/26.

claim: The deployed commander authorizes R&R Leave
quote: Rest and Recuperation leave programs are applicable only in combat areas and must be approved by the Assistant Secretary of Defense.
fix: R&R programs are approved at ASD level and locations are designated through the GCCDR. Say so and cite DoDI 1327.06 CH 1 para 3.10.i.

claim: R&R chargeable rules differ from annual leave
quote: travel time shall not be charged to the Marine’s leave account. However, the actual period of time in the R&R area shall be charged

claim: Marine must reach a deployment duration threshold for R&R eligibility
quote: R&R leave will only be granted to Service members that are deployed to a designated R&R duty location for at least 12 months.
fix: Name the threshold. DoDI 1327.06 CH 1 sets 12 months and MCO 1050.3J ch 2 para 13.c sets more than 90 days (60 at a contingency location). Reconcile.

claim: Terminal leave runs continuously including weekends and holidays, over 90 days needs CMC approval, overseas Marines may request up to 60 days before tour completion
quote: Leave in excess of 90 days may not be granted without prior authorization from the CMC (MMEA/MMOA, or RA, as applicable).

claim: The Marine agrees to notify the commander holding the records of location on the separation date so the DD 214 can be mailed
quote: The Marine must agree to notify the commander having custody of the service records

claim: Marines absent on leave at separation are charged leave for the last day of active duty
quote: will be charged leave for the last day of active duty.

claim: Run DD Form 2648 pre-separation counseling per MCO 1900.16 before terminal leave departure
quote: Completion of the the Pre-separation Counseling Checklist, DD Form 2648 (Regular component)

claim: Terminal leave for federal employment is authorized and the leave authorization carries the statement Separation Leave, 5 U.S.C., section 5534a
quote: Separation Leave, 5 U.S.C., section 5534a

claim: S-1 officer signs by direction on routine terminal leave orders
quote: Upon request, commanders may grant leave up to the extent of accrued leave.
fix: Paragraph 24.a puts the grant with commanders. By direction signature is a local practice, not an order requirement.

claim: DoD FMR Vol 7A Chapter 35 paragraph 2.1.1.2 sets the 60-day lifetime sell-back cap
fix: Vol 7A Chapter 35 is not in the cluster archive. The cap itself is in MCO 1050.3J ch 2 para 2.b and Title 37 USC 501. Verify the paragraph number.
